title: MiniQMT managed batch submit lacks full-batch preflight retry and compensation workflow
description:
Expected: Before submitting a multi-order miniQMT strategy batch, AIstock should run a full-batch preflight that validates every item, aggregate cash/can-sell constraints, duplicate symbols/order_remark collisions, and idempotent retry semantics. If any item fails before broker submit, no broker orders should be sent. If broker submission partially succeeds, the API must persist a clear batch status and provide explicit compensation/cancel workflow rather than only a textual hint.
Actual: QmtManagedOrderService.submit_batch() currently executes submit_order sequentially. If some orders succeed and a later order fails, broker orders already exist and the result only sets compensation_required with hint 'review accepted broker orders; no automatic cancel was issued'. Raw batch endpoint is also non-atomic. This behavior is documented as residual POC risk, but it is not sufficient for stable multi-strategy strategy-package execution.
reproduce_command: rg -n "def submit_batch|compensation_required|no automatic cancel|orders/batch|order_batch|batch_status|partial" backend/services/qmt_strategy_ledger backend/routers/qmt_strategy_ledger.py backend/routers/qmt.py backend/tests/qmt_strategy_ledger docs/architecture/miniqmt_multi_strategy_execution_implementation_plan_20260518.md -S
required_verification: Unit test: if any item fails full-batch preflight, zero broker place_order calls occur.
Unit test: full-batch preflight aggregates cash, duplicate order_remark, same-symbol sell availability, and broker can_sell constraints where applicable.
Unit test: broker partial success persists batch PARTIAL state and exposes compensation/cancel actions or explicit operator instructions.
Unit test: idempotent retry of the same batch does not create duplicate order_intent or duplicate broker orders.
Router/API test: batch response clearly separates preflight failure, broker partial success, and completed success.
closure_requirements: Batch submit uses a two-phase plan: validate all requests before broker submission, then submit with auditable item status.
Partial broker success has persisted state and an explicit compensation workflow.
Duplicate retry semantics are defined and tested.
The implementation does not claim impossible broker-side atomicity, but prevents avoidable pre-broker partial submission.

events.note: Root cause hypothesis: batch service was implemented as sequential single-order submissions with post-hoc partial success reporting, not as a two-phase full-batch preflight plus explicit broker-submit plan.
Business impact: P1 because partial broker success can leave account and strategy ledger in a state that requires manual compensation, especially when running 20+ symbols per strategy.

This issue should not promise impossible broker atomicity. The product requirement is deterministic pre-broker all-or-nothing validation, persisted batch state, idempotent retry, and explicit operator compensation for broker-side partial success.

Required verification: preflight failure in any item causes zero broker calls; successful preflight submits all items; broker partial success persists batch PARTIAL state and exposes cancel/compensation actions.
Required verification: duplicate order_remark/idempotent retry behavior is defined and tested for same batch reruns.
